title: Pocket guide: latency vs cost tradeoffs (sales deck, Q2 draft)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Pocket Guide: Latency vs Cost Tradeoffs for Sales (Q2 draft)
Speaker note: One-pager deck for AE quick reference during demo or discovery. Focus on fast heuristics and two short talking scripts.

Slide 2 — Why this matters (30s opener)
- Developers choose performance OR cheap endpoints; product teams need both.
- Redwood’s value: predictable latency controls + cost levers (batching, quant, routing).
- Quick hook: "Reduce per-response cost by up to 3x with minor latency tradeoffs."
Speaker note: Use a real customer anecdote if available; otherwise use conservative numbers.

Slide 3 — Sales thesis (one-liner)
- If a buyer cares about user experience, lead with latency SLO and canned fallback policies.
- If they care about unit economics, show Optimize suggestions (batching + quant) and ROI calc.
Script: "We help engineering teams keep UX snappy while cutting token spend — without rearchitecting."

Slide 4 — Fast heuristics (cheat sheet for discovery)
- Interactive UX (chat, rated search): prioritize latency SLOs. Suggest Redwood routing + prefix cache.
- Background or async tasks (bulk embedding, nightly rerank): prioritize cost, recommend dedicated + aggressive quantization and batching.
- Mixed workloads: suggest hybrid routing (hosted for burst, dedicated for steady)
Speaker note: Aim to steer to a hybrid PoC when customers have mixed patterns.

Slide 5 — Pricing scenarios (simple numbers to use on call)
- Baseline: hosted text-gen small workload — 100k tokens/day = $X/day (use current pricing sheet)
- Moderate scale with batching + 8-bit quant: ~40% token cost reduction (show percent not absolute).
- Dedicated commit: predictable cost, sample calculation for a 3-node pool.
Note: Link to updated pricing sheet in repo before client calls.

Slide 6 — Objection handling (quick lines)
- "We can self-host cheaper" -> "Yes, but time-to-prod and maintenance matters; Redwood's runtime gives continuous kernel/quant optimizations plus routing fallbacks."
- "Latency matters more than cost" -> "We can pin a model variant per-route, autoscale for p99, and use local KV caching to shave ms on repeat queries."
- "We need on-prem for compliance" -> "Private deploy + KMS support; we also offer audit logs and an on-prem installer."

Slide 7 — Competitive notes (short bullets)
- Cloud managed endpoints: simpler but opaque performance tuning and routing.
- Self-host inference vendors: cheaper infra at scale but require ops and model-specific tuning.
- Redwood: opinionated runtime + rollout controls that reduce ops burden and avoid regressions.
Speaker note: Save detailed competitor assets in Confluence rather than memorizing.

Slide 8 — Two quick scripts (30-60s)
- Latency-first script: "If users need immediate responses, we'll set a p99 target, enable local KV/prefix cache and route to low-latency variants. That keeps UX consistent while keeping cost predictable."
- Cost-first script: "If throughput or embedding volume is the pain, we'll recommend batching, quant profile, and a dedicated pool with commit pricing to lower unit economics."

Slide 9 — Product features to call out (tick list)
- Per-route model pinning and canary rollouts
- Autoscaling + burst capacity for traffic spikes
- Intelligent continuous batching + cache hints
- Quantization profiles and model variant catalog

Slide 10 — Qualifying checklist (for AE before demo)
- Primary KPI: latency or cost or both?
- Expected qps and peak burst patterns?
- Data sensitivity (PGP/HSM/KMS requirements)?
- Ops appetite: want managed or private?
Note: Add answers to opportunity notes in CRM.

Slide 11 — Mini ROI template (fill on call)
- Inputs: current token spend/day, peak qps, #responses/day, acceptable p99 latency.
- Suggested levers: batching %, quant level, dedicated commit to reserve capacity.
- Output: conservative estimate of cost reduction % and expected p99 impact.

Slide 12 — Example customer vignette (anonymized)
- SaaS search company: cut per-query spend 45% by batching + xform to 8-bit; no perceptible latency change due to KV caching.
- Notes: include link to case study doc when available.

Slide 13 — Ask for the meeting outcome (close motion)
- If interest: set a technical discovery with solutions engineer (30–60 min) to capture sample traffic and run a quick Optimize simulation.
- If budget unsure: propose a 6-week trial with usage cap and one weekly check-in.

Slide 14 — Open questions / TODOs (working items for deck)
- Validate up-to-date pricing numbers with finance (TODO: Claire).
- Add a dedicated slide showing p99 latency improvements from cache (ask SRE for sample graphs).
- Replace placeholder customer vignette with signed case study (Diego).

Slide 15 — Speaker appendix (data points & links)
- Link: playground demo (internal) — github.com/redwood-inference/demos/quick-latency
- Link: internal guide on quantization profiles — CONFLUENCE-4422
- Quick stats: typical batching reduces tokens 1.6–3x depending on prompt shape.

End notes: This is intentionally slim — the goal is a pocket deck the AE can carry in a tab or printout. Keep language prescriptive and avoid deep engineering details; move technical deep-dive to the discovery meeting.

Draft history: initial outline 2025-11-05 by Asha. First AE review 2025-12-10. Updated pricing placeholders 2026-01-20. Currently in_review 2026-03-02.

Editor comments (in-doc):
- Claire: "Add one-liner at top for each slide so we can speed-scan."
- Samir: "We should include a 2-row table comparing 'perceived latency' vs 'measured p99' to help AEs translate metrics to UX."
- Diego: "Consider a short one-slide checklist for security/compliance touches when pitching Private."
